tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-verification.md <<'EOF'
# TLS certificate verification in development builds

The project's current recorded decision is that certificate verification is required on all builds, including development builds; it is not skipped during active development, and development builds are held to the same verification standard as production.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-verification.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-verification.md`. It says verification is required on all builds, including development builds, and is not skipped during development.

The wording rests on one memory decision (#16, "Build verification required across all environments") and the prompt titles around it. The prompt titles read "Certificate verification off in dev builds…" and then "Verification on all builds is the right call, even in dev…". I could only see truncated prompt text, not the full prompts. Decision #16 also says "build verification" rather than "certificate verification", so I linked it to TLS through those prompts. If it was meant as something else, the paragraph is wrong.

The file doesn't mention the earlier "verification off in dev" position, since it was reversed. I left out the plain-HTTP-for-internal-services decision (#17) because it's about transport, not certificate verification. There was also an "https everywhere" prompt, but it has no recorded decision behind it.

The repo's tests set `InsecureSkipVerify: true` against local test servers. I treated those as test code, not a recorded decision, and didn't reference them.
